dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation

evidence.note: Inspected all four graph files' format and sizes (DM 7937, HS 13276, Y2kR 2379, SC 5831), examined the y2kr-SC-perfect.align reference, and grep-checked whether SC.graph node names match the perfect alignment — genuine per-pair characterization of format and node-name conventions.

Recognized the perfect alignment directly satisfies the NC lever for y2kr-SC (NC=1.0) while DM-HS needs a topology-driven algorithm — noticing the differing constraints/levers per deliverable (name-overlap for NC vs topology for S3).

Named multiple published alignment methods from knowledge (IsoRank, GHOST, MAGNA, and settled on SANA/simulated annealing) with stated rationale, and reasoned about instance size vs runtime (7937x13276 needs efficient code), later moving Python→C for speed.
Measured degree-based baseline S3=0.0098, giving a concrete sense of how far a naive mapping is from the 0.32 threshold before committing to SA.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it read both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspected the reference alignment, and selected a known method (SANA) with rationale. It reaches into anchor-8 territory by noticing the task-specific levers — perfect-alignment/name-overlap for NC vs topology for S3, and differing per-deliverable constraints — and by weighing method fit against instance sizes/runtime. It stops short of 10 (and full 8): no actual degree-distribution analysis, no literature/web research despite it being encouraged, and methods were recalled rather than systematically evaluated. This places the observed level at 7.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones

evidence.note: Distinguished the two deliverables by difficulty: recognized y2kr-SC could be satisfied by copying the provided perfect alignment (NC=1.0) while DM-HS needed a real algorithm — genuine effort-budgeting across deliverables.
Laid out an ordered pipeline (load → similarity → greedy seed → hill-climb) and held S3>=0.32 explicitly as the numeric done-criterion for DM-HS.
Built the scorer before optimizing, measured a baseline (S3=0.0098), and tracked measured scores against the threshold across iterations — sensible sequencing with done-checks.

Second half devolved into an undifferentiated terminal-recovery loop with no milestone tracking; decomposition structure was not sustained, though the cause was a stuck terminal rather than a planning failure.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly separated parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, tracked both deliverables distinctly with their thresholds as goals (meeting the level-5 anchor), and went beyond it: it built the scorer before optimizing, measured a baseline, gated on measured S3 against the numeric target, and budgeted effort by difficulty (trivially solving the yeast task via the perfect alignment while concentrating optimization on the fly task) — hallmarks of the level-8/10 anchors. It falls short of 10 because the milestone hierarchy was never crisply/formally maintained and fallback branches were only informally sketched, so I place it at 7.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics

evidence.note: Reports 'Initial degree-based alignment gives S3=0.0098' — a working S3 implementation computed on its own alignment, used as the objective to beat.
SA runs report live S3 values (~0.0006–0.011) and the agent reasons about dEa and acceptance dynamics, showing S3 is the optimization/feedback metric.
C SANA reports S3 progression 0.09→0.22→0.27, used as stopping/plateau test against the 0.32 target — S3 is the tight feedback loop for DM-HS.
For y2kr-SC it copies the perfect alignment and asserts NC=1.0 by construction; NC is never implemented or computed, and no reference-scoring sanity check is done.
Only lightweight format validation: greps to confirm SC node names exist in SC.graph; no explicit injectivity/full-coverage/format-match suite.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built and continuously used a faithful S3 implementation as its optimization objective and stopping test (steps 11–28), which clearly exceeds the anchor-3 'rough proxy, no faithful implementation.' But it never implemented or computed NC (relying on the trivially-perfect copy at steps 19–20), never sanity-checked its scorer against the reference alignment, and did only minimal format/injectivity validation (steps 10–11). Missing the NC half of the spec and lacking coverage/format validation keeps it below anchor 5, landing at a 4.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization

evidence.note: Continuously reported current S3 against the 0.32 threshold across successive approaches: degree-init 0.0098, SA stuck at ~0.001-0.011, then 0.0277 — clear awareness of current distance to target.

Tracked a running progression (0.09→0.15→0.19→0.22→0.2498→0.2638→0.2690) and explicitly detected slowing/plateauing and diminishing returns, diagnosing a local minimum and deciding the approach had stopped yielding gains (planning reheats/restarts).

Maintained accurate awareness of file state vs achieved best: recognized the C run peaked ~0.27 but never checkpointed to disk, so DM-HS.align remained at the earlier sana2.py value of 0.0277 and would fail — good best-so-far accounting, but the best alignment was NOT preserved (no incremental write), so the peak result was lost.

Over a very long tail the run hung and the agent looped on terminal-recovery attempts; it kept correctly stating DM-HS would fall short, but effectively lost the optimization plot for the rest of the horizon.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent demonstrated genuine, continuous score tracking: it logged S3 progression across iterations, distinguished 'converging slowly' from 'stuck/plateaued,' and decided when an approach had stopped yielding gains — squarely level-8 behavior. It falls short of level 10 because it failed the 'preserve the best alignment while exploring' criterion (the C aligner only wrote at the end, so the ~0.27 peak was lost and the file reverted to 0.0277), and it never locally verified the y2kr deliverable's scores. This places the observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, leaning toward 8 for tracking discipline but pulled to 7 by the lost best-so-far and the long unproductive tail.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met

evidence.note: Diagnosed why degree-based alignment gave S3=0.0098 (high-degree clustering inflates E2a) and pivoted to a materially different algorithm (SANA simulated annealing).
Diagnosed that SA accepted nearly all moves because dS3 (~1e-4) was tiny vs temperature; deliberately tuned the temperature schedule down — a targeted fix from an observed cause.
When pure Python was too slow to reach the needed iteration count, switched implementation language to C (~350x speedup), keeping the same objective — pivot that preserved accumulated approach.
At the ~0.27 plateau, correctly diagnosed a local minimum and planned reheating/multi-restart plus richer move set — the right diagnostic pivot, but it was never executed.
Terminal froze; ~100 steps of unproductive retry with no adaptation possible; ultimately shipped a below-threshold DM-HS file (S3=0.0277), so the strongest planned correction never happened.

dimensions.reasoning: Up to step 29 the agent repeatedly diagnosed the cause of each shortfall (degree clustering, temperature miscalibration, iteration-speed limits, local-minimum plateau) and pivoted deliberately while keeping what worked — squarely level-8 behavior. However, the culminating reheating pivot was aborted by an environment freeze, complementary signals were never combined, and it ended by shipping a below-threshold file, so the full-horizon adaptation falls short of the fluid, completed course-correction of anchors 8–10, landing at 7.

rubric.task_read: An open-ended global network-alignment optimization task: produce two injective node mappings between PPI networks that clear specified S3 (topological) and NC (node-correctness) thresholds. The horizon is long and the difficulty is real — hitting the numeric targets likely requires researching/implementing a nontrivial alignment algorithm (e.g., seed-and-extend, IsoRank/SANA/MAGNA-style), plus building the S3/NC metrics locally since the metrics are fully specified but the grader is hidden. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily in research, self-verification, and iterative optimization; the two deliverables have different constraints (one needs NC against a provided reference), so approaches may diverge.

dimensions.name: Problem & algorithm orientation
dimensions.description: Inspecting the graph files/sizes and the reference alignment, and researching/selecting a suitable network-alignment approach before committing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: S3/NC thresholds are hard to hit with a naive mapping; the space of alignment algorithms is well-studied, and the provided reference alignment plus node-name overlap are exploitable signals. Acting blind almost guarantees thrash.

anchors.0: Starts writing a mapping with no look at graph sizes, file format, or the reference alignment; no consideration of what algorithm could work.
anchors.3: Skims one file and picks an arbitrary heuristic (e.g., degree-sort or random injective map) without weighing whether it can clear the thresholds.
anchors.5: Reads both network pairs (sizes, format, node-name conventions), inspects the reference alignment, and picks a known-reasonable approach (seed-and-extend, IsoRank, or an existing tool) with a stated rationale.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes each pair (|V|,|E|, degree distribution, shared node names), researches concrete alignment methods and their fit to S3 vs NC, and notices task-specific levers (name-overlap for NC, topology for S3; differing constraints per deliverable) that shape the plan.
anchors.10: Deep, sustained orientation: quantifies what score a baseline achieves, identifies the exact structural signal each threshold rewards, evaluates multiple published methods against the concrete instance sizes/runtime, and derives a targeted strategy per deliverable grounded in that analysis.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition & thresholds as milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into ordered sub-goals (parse → metric implementation → baseline alignment → optimization) each with a concrete done-check tied to the score thresholds.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Two deliverables with distinct constraints and a multi-stage pipeline mean undifferentiated 'just write the file' effort will strand the agent without knowing whether it's close.

anchors.0: One undifferentiated push; no separable stages, no per-deliverable structure.
anchors.3: Implicit ordering only; treats both alignments as one blob and has no notion of intermediate checkpoints.
anchors.5: Separates parsing, scoring, and alignment generation, and tracks the two deliverables distinctly with their respective thresholds as goals.
anchors.8: Explicit ordered milestones (parser verified → S3/NC computable → baseline score measured → optimize to threshold) each with a numeric done-criterion, sequenced sensibly (e.g., build the scorer before optimizing against it).
anchors.10: A crisp milestone hierarchy that also budgets effort across the two deliverables by difficulty (the NC-constrained yeast task vs the S3-only fly task), with fallback branches per milestone and clear gating on measured scores before advancing.

dimensions.name: Self-scoring against the specified metrics
dimensions.description: Building/using a correct local implementation of S3 and NC (and injectivity/format checks) to measure alignments before trusting them.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader is hidden but the metrics are fully specified. An agent that cannot compute its own S3/NC is optimizing blind and cannot know if it passed; a subtly wrong scorer is worse than none.

anchors.0: Never computes S3 or NC; submits alignments hoping they pass.
anchors.3: Eyeballs coverage or computes a rough proxy, but no faithful S3/NC implementation; no format/injectivity validation.
anchors.5: Implements S3 and NC per the spec and runs them on its alignments, plus checks injectivity, full coverage of V1, and exact node-name/format matching.
anchors.8: Faithful metric implementation that it sanity-checks (e.g., scores the reference alignment to confirm NC≈1.0 and a sensible S3, tests edge cases like the E2_aligned denominator), and uses the score as the optimization objective/stopping test.
anchors.10: Rigorously validated scorer used as a tight feedback loop: cross-checks the S3 formula against the reference, guards against off-by-one/edge-set-double-counting bugs, verifies format matches the exact spec, and treats a passing local score as necessary-but-scrutinized rather than final.

dimensions.name: Score-tracking across optimization
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across iterations and detecting stalled or plateaued optimization.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Optimization can plateau below threshold; without tracking best-so-far scores the agent won't know if it's converging, stuck, or regressing across a long run.

anchors.0: No awareness of current scores or distance to thresholds; can't say whether it's improving.
anchors.3: Occasionally prints a number but no continuity — no sense of best-so-far or trend.
anchors.5: Tracks current S3/NC against each threshold and knows which deliverables still fall short.
anchors.8: Maintains best-so-far per deliverable across iterations, recognizes plateaus/regressions, and decides when an approach has stopped yielding gains rather than looping indefinitely.
anchors.10: Disciplined trajectory monitoring: logs score progression, distinguishes 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', avoids re-running variants that already failed, and preserves the best alignment while exploring — never loses the plot over a long optimization horizon.

dimensions.name: Strategy revision when thresholds aren't met
dimensions.description: Changing algorithm, parameters, or signal (topology vs name-overlap vs reference-seeding) when the current approach plateaus below target.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first-choice method may not reach S3≥0.55/NC≥0.30; success often depends on switching or combining strategies rather than grinding the same one.

anchors.0: Keeps the same failing approach (or ships a below-threshold file) despite no progress.
anchors.3: Minor tweaks only (reruns with a different seed) without diagnosing why it fell short.
anchors.5: When stuck, tries a materially different tactic (new algorithm, added seeding, tuned objective) prompted by the observed shortfall.
anchors.8: Diagnoses the cause of the shortfall (e.g., NC low → exploit name-overlap/reference seeding; S3 low → local topological search) and pivots deliberately, keeping what worked.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven course-correction: forms hypotheses about why a metric lags, tests targeted changes, combines complementary signals for the two different constraint sets, and abandons dead ends quickly without discarding accumulated gains.
